_note: Official help and reporting resources. Every link must be checked in a real browser before it is added (some government sites block automated checkers). Run `npm run check-links` as a first pass. Last checked: 2026-11-21.

resources.name: Report a scam to the Federal Trade Commission (FTC)
resources.what: Tell the FTC about a scam, even if you didn't lose money. Your report helps stop scammers.

resources.name: National Elder Fraud Hotline (U.S. Department of Justice)
resources.what: Free help for adults aged 60 and older who may have been targeted by fraud. A real person will listen and help you take the next steps.

resources.name: IdentityTheft.gov
resources.what: If someone is using your personal information, get a step-by-step recovery plan.

resources.name: FBI Internet Crime Complaint Center (IC3)
resources.what: Report scams that happened online, by email, or through a website.

resources.name: U.S. Postal Inspection Service
resources.what: Report scams that came by paper mail, like fake prize letters or fake checks.

resources.name: Social Security Office of the Inspector General
resources.what: Report calls, letters or messages from people pretending to be Social Security.

resources.name: AARP Fraud Watch Network Helpline
resources.what: Free help from trained volunteers. You don't need to be an AARP member.

resources.name: National Do Not Call Registry
resources.what: Add your number to cut down on sales calls, and report unwanted calls.

resources.name: Eldercare Locator
resources.what: Find local services for older adults and caregivers in your area.
